title: Server Hardware
description: Is the server hardware healthy: temperatures, fans, power supplies, batteries, power draw, room in the BMCs' event logs, and add-in GPUs?

panels.title: BMCs not answering
panels.description: Servers whose BMC didn't answer every collector at the last scrape. Their sensors aren't being checked.

panels.title: Critical sensors
panels.description: Sensors in critical state: a failed battery, power supply or fan, or a reading past its critical limit. Empty slots and Supermicro's LED pattern sensors don't count. Details in Sensors not nominal.

targets.expr: count({__name__=~"ipmi_(sensor|temperature|fan_speed|voltage|current|power)_state", job="ipmi", host=~"$host", type!="Entity Presence", name!~"Pattern[0-9]+"} == 2) or vector(0)

panels.title: Warning sensors
panels.description: Sensors in warning state: a reading past its warning limit, or redundancy reduced.

targets.expr: count({__name__=~"ipmi_(sensor|temperature|fan_speed|voltage|current|power)_state", job="ipmi", host=~"$host", type!="Entity Presence", name!~"Pattern[0-9]+"} == 1) or vector(0)

panels.title: Power draw
panels.description: What the selected servers draw together, from each BMC's live (DCMI) power reading.

panels.title: Hottest inlet
panels.description: The warmest air going into a server: Dell's Inlet Temp, Supermicro's System Temp. Orange from 30 °C, red from 38 °C.

panels.title: Event log space left
panels.description: Free space in the fullest BMC event log. At zero the BMC records no new hardware events: save the log and clear it.

panels.title: Servers
panels.description: One row per server. BMC: whether every collector could read it. Power: the BMC's live (DCMI) reading. Inlet: Dell's Inlet Temp or Supermicro's System Temp. Hottest CPU: Dell's CPU sensors are named Temp, Supermicro's CPUn Temp. Sensors not OK: in warning or critical state, not counting empty slots (Entity Presence) or Supermicro's LED pattern sensors. A BMC stops recording events when its event log is full.

targets.expr: max by (host) (ipmi_temperature_celsius{job="ipmi", host=~"$host", name=~"Inlet Temp|System Temp"})

count by (host) ({__name__=~"ipmi_(sensor|temperature|fan_speed|voltage|current|power)_state", job="ipmi", host=~"$host", type!="Entity Presence", name!~"Pattern[0-9]+"} > 0) or on (host) (max by (host) (ipmi_up{job="ipmi", host=~"$host"}) * 0)
max by (host, manufacturer_id, firmware_revision, system_firmware_version) (ipmi_bmc_info{job="ipmi", host=~"$host"})

panels.title: Sensors not nominal
panels.description: Every sensor the BMCs report in warning or critical state, the same ones the Hardware sensor alerts watch: empty slots (Entity Presence) and Supermicro's PatternN LED sensors are left out.

targets.expr: max by (host, name, id, type) ({__name__=~"ipmi_(sensor|temperature|fan_speed|voltage|current|power)_state", job="ipmi", host=~"$host", type!="Entity Presence", name!~"Pattern[0-9]+"} > 0)

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description: Every temperature sensor. Dell names its CPU sensors Temp, so the sensor id tells them apart.

panels.title: Fan speed
panels.description: Every fan the BMCs report.

panels.title: Power draw
panels.description: Each server's live (DCMI) power reading.

panels.title: Event log entries
panels.description: Entries in each BMC's event log. A jump means the BMC logged hardware events; a drop, that the log was cleared.

panels.title: Hottest GPU
panels.description: The warmest add-in GPU that the server's own driver reads (Intel i915 or xe, through node_exporter's hwmon collector; the BMC can't see these cards). Orange from 80 °C, red from 85 °C, where the GPU hot alert starts counting.

panels.title: GPU temperature
panels.description: Each add-in GPU's temperature, named by its PCI address. The dashed line is the GPU hot alert's 85 °C (it fires after 10 minutes above it). If the card is passed through to a VM, the VM reports it instead of the server.

targets.expr: max by (host, chip, gpu) (label_replace(node_hwmon_temp_celsius{host=~"$host"} * on (job, host, chip) group_left node_hwmon_chip_names{chip_name=~"i915|xe", host=~"$host"}, "gpu", "$1.$2", "chip", ".*([0-9a-f]{4}:[0-9a-f]{2}:[0-9a-f]{2})_([0-9a-f])"))

panels.title: GPU power
panels.description: Each add-in GPU's power draw, from the energy counter its driver keeps, and its power limit (dashed): the sustained draw the driver holds the card to. A card near its limit is busy, transcoding for example; a card that runs hot at low power is short of airflow.

targets.expr: max by (host, chip, gpu) (label_replace(rate(node_hwmon_energy_joule_total{host=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]) * on (job, host, chip) group_left node_hwmon_chip_names{chip_name=~"i915|xe", host=~"$host"}, "gpu", "$1.$2", "chip", ".*([0-9a-f]{4}:[0-9a-f]{2}:[0-9a-f]{2})_([0-9a-f])"))

max by (host, chip, gpu) (label_replace(node_hwmon_power_max_watt{host=~"$host"} * on (job, host, chip) group_left node_hwmon_chip_names{chip_name=~"i915|xe", host=~"$host"}, "gpu", "$1.$2", "chip", ".*([0-9a-f]{4}:[0-9a-f]{2}:[0-9a-f]{2})_([0-9a-f])"))

panels.title: GPU fan speed
panels.description: The add-in GPUs' own fans. The server's fans don't speed up for a third-party card, so this fan and the server's airflow are all it has.

targets.expr: max by (host, chip, gpu) (label_replace(node_hwmon_fan_rpm{host=~"$host"} * on (job, host, chip) group_left node_hwmon_chip_names{chip_name=~"i915|xe", host=~"$host"}, "gpu", "$1.$2", "chip", ".*([0-9a-f]{4}:[0-9a-f]{2}:[0-9a-f]{2})_([0-9a-f])"))

panels.title: Intel GPUs
panels.description: Every Intel GPU that Argus' Intel GPU exporter finds on a server's or host's PCI bus, and whether it reports load. Reporting: the server's own i915 driver has the GPU and intel_gpu_top reads it. Not reporting: i915 has it but intel_gpu_top can't read it (the Intel GPU not reporting alert). Not sampled: another driver has it; vfio-pci means it's passed through to a VM, which reports it under its own name when it runs the agent's intel-gpu profile.

targets.expr: (max by (host, pci_slot, driver) (intel_gpu_info{job="intel_gpu", host=~"$host"}) + on (host, pci_slot) group_left () max by (host, pci_slot) (intel_gpu_up{job="intel_gpu", host=~"$host"})) or max by (host, pci_slot, driver) (intel_gpu_info{job="intel_gpu", host=~"$host"}) * 0

panels.title: Intel GPU engine load
panels.description: How busy each Intel GPU's engines are, by intel_gpu_top (the i915 driver's counters): Render/3D (also tone mapping and filters), Video (decode and encode, Quick Sync: what Plex, Jellyfin and Tdarr use) and VideoEnhance (scaling and deinterlacing). The share of time busy over each interval, so short bursts aren't missed between scrapes. The card's power is on GPU power above.

panels.title: Intel GPU clock
panels.description: Each Intel GPU's actual clock, and the clock the driver asked for (dashed). An idle card sits at its lowest clock or in RC6; a card that gets less than it asks for is held back by power or temperature.

panels.title: Intel GPU idle (RC6)
panels.description: The share of time each Intel GPU spends in RC6, its low-power idle state. Near 100 % on a card with nothing to do; a card that never gets there is kept awake.
